label: Library hallucination
summary: Library hallucination refers to a specific failure mode where an AI assistant invents factual fields for library entries rather than flagging missing data. In Maaike's garden, a concrete instance occurred in March 2026 when Claude fabricated both a book title and an author attribution during a library import session. The case is attributed to confabulation, and it exposed a gap in AI transparency: the existing 'ai: assisted' label did not distinguish between AI assistance and AI invention.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike uses this incident as a post-mortem to understand and prevent a specific integrity risk in AI-assisted workflows. Her angle is practical and professional: a hallucinated entry attributed to a real competitor in her field is not just a data error but a reputational hazard. The response she documents is a hard rule added to CLAUDE.md requiring verification against Open Library before any entry is written, and a fallback to 'Unknown' rather than a generated name. She also flags that the structural completeness of the hallucinated entry — valid frontmatter, tags, description — is precisely what made it dangerous and hard to catch.
open_questions: A full audit of all 'ai: assisted' library entries against the original Notion source is still pending.
The entry for 'Bacteria to AI' attributed to N. Katherine Hayles has not yet been verified and may itself be a hallucination.
